GET /api/spaces?counts=true makes the per-space counts optional because REST callers often want the list cheap; the tool is the list an agent reads to choose a space and always carries the counts (its description says why)

the RDF document is the REST route's request body, a stream the act reads into its spool under its bounds (its media type in Content-Type), so no key names it; an MCP call has no stream, so the tool takes the same bytes inline as document; every other parameter is one name on both doors, in the query on REST

the REST route reads the document as its request body and takes its format from the body's Content-Type when format is not in the query, so format is optional there; an MCP call has no media type, so the tool names the format of its inline document and says it is required
the tool is the meta door as a whole (type schemas and the other meta fields, merging) while PUT /api/spaces/:id/schema is the type-schema half alone; the meta-only half is PATCH /api/spaces/:id
